{{Short description|Algebraic geometry}}
In [[commutative algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]], a morphism is called '''formally étale''' if it has a [[lifting property]] that is analogous to being a [[local diffeomorphism]].

== Formally étale homomorphisms of rings ==
Let ''A'' be a [[topological ring]], and let ''B'' be a topological ''A''-algebra. Then ''B'' is '''formally étale''' if for all [[discrete topology|discrete]] ''A''-algebras ''C'', all [[nilpotent ideal]]s ''J'' of ''C'', and all continuous ''A''-homomorphisms {{nowrap|''u'' : ''B'' → ''C''/''J''}}, there exists a unique continuous ''A''-algebra map {{nowrap|''v'' : ''B'' → ''C''}} such that {{nowrap|''u'' {{=}} ''pv''}}, where {{nowrap|''p'' : ''C'' → ''C''/''J''}} is the canonical projection.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV1|EGA 0<sub>IV</sub>]], Définition 19.10.2.</ref>

Formally étale is equivalent to [[formally smooth]] plus [[formally unramified]].<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV1|EGA 0<sub>IV</sub>]], Définition 19.10.2.</ref>

== Formally étale morphisms of schemes ==
Since the [[structure sheaf]] of a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] naturally carries only the discrete topology, the notion of formally étale for schemes is analogous to formally étale for the discrete topology for rings.  That is, a morphism of schemes {{nowrap|''f'' : ''X'' → ''Y''}}  is '''formally étale''' if for every affine ''Y''-scheme ''Z'', every [[nilpotent ideal|nilpotent]] [[sheaf of ideals]] ''J'' on ''Z'' with {{nowrap|''i'' : ''Z''<sub>0</sub> → ''Z''}} be the closed immersion determined by ''J'', and every ''Y''-morphism {{nowrap|''g'' : ''Z''<sub>0</sub> → ''X''}}, there exists a unique ''Y''-morphism {{nowrap|''s'' : ''Z'' → ''X''}} such that {{nowrap|''g'' {{=}} ''si''}}.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], Définition 17.1.1.</ref>

It is equivalent to let ''Z'' be any ''Y''-scheme and let ''J'' be a [[locally nilpotent]] sheaf of ideals on ''Z''.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], Remarques 17.1.2 (iv).</ref>

== Properties ==
*[[Open immersion]]s are formally étale.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], proposition 17.1.3 (i).</ref>
*The property of being formally étale is preserved under composites, base change, and [[fibered product]]s.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], proposition 17.1.3 (ii)–(iv).</ref>
*If {{nowrap|''f'' : ''X'' → ''Y''}} and {{nowrap|''g'' : ''Y'' → ''Z''}} are morphisms of schemes, ''g'' is formally unramified, and ''gf'' is formally étale, then ''f'' is formally étale.  In particular, if ''g'' is formally étale, then ''f'' is formally étale if and only if ''gf'' is.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], proposition 17.1.4 and corollaire 17.1.5.</ref>
* The property of being formally étale is [[local property#Properties of commutative rings|local]] on the source and target.<ref>[[#Reference-EGAIV4|EGA IV<sub>4</sub>]], proposition 17.1.6.</ref>
* The property of being formally étale can be checked on stalks.  One can show that a morphism of rings {{nowrap|''f'' : ''A'' → ''B''}} is formally étale if and only if for every prime ''Q'' of ''B'', the induced map {{nowrap|''A'' → ''B''<sub>''Q''</sub>}} is formally étale.<ref>[https://mathoverflow.net/q/16132 mathoverflow.net question]</ref>  Consequently, ''f'' is formally étale if and only if for every prime ''Q'' of ''B'', the map {{nowrap|''A''<sub>''P''</sub> → ''B''<sub>''Q''</sub>}} is formally étale, where {{nowrap|''P'' {{=}} ''f''<sup>&minus;1</sup>(''Q'')}}.

== Examples ==
*[[Localization of a ring|Localizations]] are formally étale.
*Finite separable field extensions are formally étale. More generally, any (commutative) [[flat module|flat]] [[separable algebra|separable ''A''-algebra]] ''B'' is formally étale.<ref>{{harvtxt|Ford|2017|loc=Corollary 4.7.3}}</ref>
